correctness.rationale: Tree series-resistance identity gives max reciprocal leaf-pair sums. Exact normalization turns the budget into a lower bound on the objective given all pair-sum constraints. Either every normalized reciprocal resistance is at most one half or precisely one is above; strict coordinate monotonicity and a strictly convex one-variable cost give the sole minimizers. Rescaling attains the lower bound and proves unique global conductances. Exact 21 reduced-Laplacian checks, 54 nonlinear convex comparisons and 8100 sampled alternatives verify examples only, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary conference full text (2006) and journal version (2008) have been compared by scientific implication. They supply tree resistance identities and a general maximum-resistance convex SDP, not the exact heterogeneously priced star design or price-threshold classification. The equal-price star calculation there concerns total resistance, not resistance diameter. Semantic-index and open-literature queries yielded no covering result. General convex solvability is acknowledged; specialized prior exact solutions may exist outside inspected sources.

value.rationale: Resistance diameter is a natural worst-pair robustness objective. The result gives a complete exact globally unique design for all sizes and arbitrary positive prices, reveals a non-obvious threshold at maximal price equal to the total of all others, proves all non-maximal edges remain equally weighted regardless of their heterogeneous prices, and gives a sharp nearly twofold performance bound relative to uniform conductance. Its comparison with published total-resistance star optimization clarifies why this exact minimax invariant matters.
